plan.understanding: Add an accessible sliding on/off switch centered on the customer-defined bottom of the housing.

subtasks.goal: Modify only housing body s0 by cutting the mounting cavity for the bottom switch; do not create or unite any actuator material in this sub-goal. Use the measured existing switch body s1 as the cavity-tool source because its bbox gives the required approximately 4.997 mm X width and 14.061 mm Z length, with its measured feature center near [27.9, 22.101, 51.27] mm. Make a transformed tool copy, turn it from its current top-facing orientation to bottom-facing so it extends inward in +Y from the housing minimum-Y surface, and position its nominal actuator center at approximately [27.9, 2.16, 51.27] mm on the bottom BSPLINE region. Form the cutter as the swept envelope of that transformed switch geometry over a small nonzero translation along world Z, so the resulting non-circular opening and internal clearance support two distinct slider positions while retaining long sides parallel to Z. Subtract that swept tool only from s0 and retain s1 unchanged. Confirm that s0 volume strictly decreases, the overall housing bbox remains unchanged, the opening is on the minimum-Y side near the specified center, and its long-axis angle is 0 degrees relative to world Z rather than 90 degrees; print the opening center and angle.

Add the bottom sliding actuator as a new separate solid without performing any further subtraction. Create a rigid transformed copy of the measured existing switch body s1, whose bbox is approximately 4.997 mm in X by 14.061 mm in Z, using the same bottom-facing transform and cavity alignment established by the preceding cut. Place it at the nominal position centered approximately at [27.9, 2.16, 51.27] mm, with its exposed outer surface at the existing minimum-Y coordinate y=2.16 mm, its thickness extending inward in +Y, and its sliding direction parallel to world Z. Keep the copied actuator separate from s0 and confirm there is no solid overlap with the housing. Demonstrate that it can be translated to two distinct positions along Z within the swept cavity while remaining inside the unchanged part envelope. Print the achieved actuator center, outermost Y coordinate, and sliding/opening long-axis angle, correcting the transform in the same attempt if the center is materially displaced or the angle is 90 degrees instead of 0 degrees.
